text.p: Winterthur Swiss Insurance Co formally launched its Shanghai subsidiary on Monday, becoming the first licensed European insurer in the China market.
The wholly owned unit will conduct non-life insurance business and focus on corporate clients, including multi-nationals, Winterthur chairman Peter Spalti told reporters.
The subsidiary has working capital of 120 million yuan ($14.5 million) and is registered in Shanghai's Pudong district, an area where Chinese authorities have been trying to speed development.
China's insurance market once was virtually monopolised by the state-owned People's Insurance Group but the sector has gradually opened up to domestic as well as foreign competition.

Besides Winterthur, only a handful of companies are able to write insurance policies in China, including American International Assurance Co Ltd, which is part of the American International Group, Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd and a Hong Kong unit of Manufacturers Life Insurance Co of Canada, which has a joint venture life insurance operation.
Chinese officials have said Germany's Allianz Group has been cleared for a licence.
Spalti said the decision to focus on non-life business probably helped accelerate permission from government, adding that there was less competition in that area.
"Non-life was much faster for a licence," he said.
He said China would eventually play a big role in the company's development but he declined to estimate future premiums.
The executive said, however, that Winterthur was not looking for high premium volume through aggressive selling but rather for quality business.
